findings.where: Article specimen: the list bullets and the PDF link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' under the hairline, at both widths
findings.fault: A red-orange appears that is in neither the palette nor the house colours. Directly above, the palette says 'four colours and no accent' and 'house blue: links'. Every other link on the page is blue ('Play again'), so the article has two link colours, and an orange that has no job against the blue brand.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked that every tile be built in or around #0070C0 and #404040 and allowed at most one accent. Angélique would also object, because when she adds articles she cannot tell which colour a link should be.

findings.where: First screen: the blue field behind the nav, heading, tags and action, at both widths (compare the Texture swatch and the motion-sketch field below)
findings.fault: Diagonal pale hatching covers the hero field. It runs behind the heading and lead text, and its ground looks busy and drafted, like a blueprint hatch. The tile's own Texture panel says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient', and the motion-sketch field is flat. One field is shown two different ways, and the hero is the busier one.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first. The brief asked for one quiet field of blue, and he finds 'techy' and busy grounds wrong for Mark. Mark himself dislikes busy sites (§6). The specimen and the hero also disagree, so he can't tell which one is being proposed.

findings.where: First screen: the ghosted 'PPP' letters in a lighter blue behind the heading (on phone, the 'PP' behind the heading at the right edge)
findings.fault: A second, paler blue sits in giant letters directly under the white heading. The heading's ground becomes two blues where the lines cross it, which muddies Mark's line. It is also a colour step with no role in the palette, which lists four colours.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. The heading is Mark's own voice and should sit cleanly on one field. A watermark of a buzzword behind it reads as a decorative trick any consultancy could use, not a refined advisor's page.

findings.where: Nav lockup on the blue field, and the Texture swatch: the aqueduct mark and 'MMM INFRA' turned all white
findings.fault: The logo is shown in a reversed white version that Mark does not hold. The logo is blue and grey, and nobody has asked whether a white version is allowed. The tile presents this as settled ('the mark reverses to white on it').
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo it is. A recoloured version needs his yes before the founder can pick a direction whose whole first screen depends on it.
